searchText: Hello, I have a question on the withdrawal functions. Is there the ability to specify a different withdrawal address for rewards and for the 32 ETH principle directly on the validator? Or is this something you have to with a proxy smart contract used as withdrawal address? you can only specify 1 address and it can't be updated. if you specify a smart contract , it won't be able to trigger any code ok, thanks. This is news to me, interesting. Why has this decision been made? With this, it is not as easily possible as it is on delegated PoS setups, to have the service provider getting some parts of the staking rewards and the delegator getting the rest. i've written it up! haha https://offchain.medium.com/deposits-locked-withdrawals-minted-a7e975708b3d but a more official official faq https://notes.ethereum.org/@launchpad/withdrawals-faq well you can it just takes another transaction, the withdrawal itself just can't trigger it ok, makes sense. Thanks a lot for your help, will check out your write-up as well There were 2 invalid deposits in the last two days on mainnet — any chance this was you or is there an unknown bug going around😩

excerpts.content: Hello, I have a question on the withdrawal functions. Is there the ability to specify a different withdrawal address for rewards and for the 32 ETH principle directly on the validator? Or is this something you have to with a proxy smart contract used as withdrawal address?

excerpts.author: jameshe5018
excerpts.content: you can only specify 1 address and it can't be updated. if you specify a smart contract , it won't be able to trigger any code

excerpts.author: camplefield
excerpts.content: ok, thanks. This is news to me, interesting. Why has this decision been made?

excerpts.author: camplefield
excerpts.content: With this, it is not as easily possible as it is on delegated PoS setups, to have the service provider getting some parts of the staking rewards and the delegator getting the rest.
